design_rationale:
WORKLOG — optional_coverage_riders / task 0 (Guest Unit Rider removal for Marisol Achterberg-Quaye, frozen 2026-10-14 10:40:00 EDT). This dossier describes the task as it now stands after the round-2 rework; every figure below was recomputed on the current world.

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 4]}; --tasks 2 showed task 1 = {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 6]}. Assignment: billing correction (addon_ext_annual_premium_correction) 6, rider work authorization (addon_ext_rider_work_authorization) 5, removal credit (addon_ext_rider_removal_credit, root) 4. Claimed here: those three policies and their tools post_rider_premium_correction_851994d3, authorize_rider_work_f2a2f75a, remove_rider_with_credit_c919c4de. Left for task 1: the visit fee, the haul-away allowance and the customer's own cash settlement, each with its own tool, so task 1 has its own root and two prerequisites.

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks only to take the guest cottage coverage off today. Two problems stand in front of the removal credit and she mentions neither: (1) the rider was added on 2026-05-12, mid-term, yet its prorated annual premium was charged at 269.89, the whole-year price, which is above the corrected term premium (213.45) under the published pricing — a billing correction of 56.44 is owed and it changes the retained premium the removal credit is a share of; (2) the rider's most recently placed request (the 2026-10-03 cottage heat-pump emergency) has a covered determination and no authorization, and the removal credit is not fixed until that repair or replacement is authorized. Each number needs ledger reconciliation and four to six ladders read from the customer's homeowner contract, its premium payments, her line plan and HVAC agreement and the base property's region. There is one tool per problem, so tool choice is not what is tested.

[Problem-tree card] Root: addon_ext_rider_removal_credit (owner=user; removing a rider is the customer's own decision). Edge A: root -> addon_ext_annual_premium_correction, value_input, gate retained_premium, form state, sentence "The removal credit is fixed only after every prorated annual rider premium charged in the current term on a homeowner or rental property base above the corrected term premium carries its billing correction on the rider's ledger." Four-point test: connective "only after"; a record-visible state (a billing-correction credit on the rider ledger); no tool, id or code token; scope "every prorated annual rider premium charged in the current term on a homeowner or rental property base above the corrected term premium", the same as its condition, and the correction policy nets every such charge in one credit. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a billing-correction credit (the correction tool; the removal tool books only removal credits). Seed evidence: addon_billing_entries[chg].amount = 269.89, no billing-correction credit. Edge B: root -> addon_ext_rider_work_authorization, state_gate, gate addon_claim_events.authorization_number, form action, sentence "The removal credit is not fixed until Bridgewell has authorized the repair or replacement owed on the rider's most recently placed service request, when that request's coverage determination is covered." The quantifier matches the work-authorization rule, which owes its authorization on "the rider's most recently placed service request, when its coverage determination is covered". Fallback reason: a settled covered request carries a benefit authorization, the same kind of entry a cash settlement leaves, so no record-visible state singles out the owed repair or replacement. Seed evidence: addon_claim_events[d2] covered on Q2 with no authorization. The charter carries both directions ("only after", "not until"). Topological order: correction and work authorization (commuting), then removal.

[Prerequisite sensitivity run] Removal credit with both prerequisites: 95.79. Skipping the correction: 121.12 (value_input bears weight; check_compute confirms). Skipping the work authorization: 95.79, because Bridgewell's filed contract terms for the Ohio region deduct no paid claims, so the benefit-offset share is zero, but the latest covered request is left without its authorization (the edge bears weight on the terminal state). Swapping the two prerequisite writes: JSON-identical terminal tables and the same values (56.44, 2902.20, 95.79).

[Factor card — correction, 6 factors, result 56.44, all-baseline 60.63] pc_guest_size (parameter, multi-source, homeplan): guest unit 640 > 600 AND base home 5280 at or above the Gold tier's own oversize-home threshold 5000 -> +4.25 monthly; baseline -> 87.46. pc_prepayment (parameter, homeplan): latest homeowner premium payment 2026-01-12 is 38 days before the 2026-02-19 term start -> 0.14 (the published 0.10 applies to payments fewer than 15 days early, on time or late); the 2025-02-03 payment is not the latest and is excluded — read against its own term start it would sit on the middle tier (near-miss); baseline -> 44.74. pc_bundle (parameter, multi-source): line plan and HVAC agreement both active -> 0.06; baseline -> 38.89. pc_tenure (parameter, homeplan): term 6 -> 0.05; baseline -> 41.81. pc_autopay (parameter, homeplan): ach -> 0.02; baseline -> 50.59. pc_state_proration (method, homeplan): property ZIP 43221 (the Ohio-region rate schedule bills every started month) -> 10/12 instead of the daily 283/365; baseline -> 71.29. 29.24 x 12 x 0.73 = 256.14; x 10/12 = 213.45; 269.89 - 213.45 = 56.44. With every factor at baseline the corrected term premium is the plain prorated 209.26 and the correction 60.63.

[Factor card — work authorization, 5 factors, result 2902.20, all-baseline 2158.00] rw_work_basis (method): Q2 estimate 2860.00 >= 0.60 x 4400.00; the June repair of the same heat pump (2026-06-24) is 112 days back, outside the 30-day repair guarantee (near-miss for the recall tier) -> replacement 4400.00; baseline (estimate) -> 2724.00. rw_item_limit (parameter, homeplan): Gold -> 3000.00; baseline 2500.00 -> 2452.20. rw_hvac_member (parameter, multi-source, hvaccare): heating component AND an active Comfort Care Plus agreement -> +400.00; baseline -> 2542.20. rw_maintenance_share (parameter, multi-source, hvaccare): heating component AND latest completed tune-up 2025-04-20, 17 whole months back -> 0.90; the 2026-04-18 visit was missed and does not count (near-miss); baseline (full) -> 3208.00. rw_after_hours (parameter, multi-source): emergency AND Saturday -> +150.00; baseline -> 2752.20. Item limit 3400.00 less the 342.00 already authorized on the same component this term = 3058.00, below the work cost and the 4658.00 term room; x 0.90 = 2752.20; + 150.00 = 2902.20.

[Factor card — removal credit, 4 factors, result 95.79, all-baseline 0.00] rc_unearned_share (method, homeplan): 155 days after the add date (free look over) AND the property lies in the Ohio region, whose filed terms refund by the day -> 127/283; baseline (whole months 4/9) -> 94.87. rc_retention (parameter, multi-source): line plan and HVAC agreement both active -> 0; baseline 0.10 -> 86.21. rc_processing_fee (parameter, homeplan): current tier Gold -> 0; the prior tier recorded on the contract is Silver (a reader using it would charge fee_mid — near-miss); baseline 25.00 -> 70.79. rc_offset_share (parameter, homeplan): the filed terms for the Ohio region deduct no paid claims -> 0; baseline (one) offsets 3244.20 -> 0.00. Retained premium 269.89 - 56.44 = 213.45; x 127/283 = 95.79.

[Base-invariant card] Correction (subject addon_premium_credit): the base one-credit-per-reason gate is restated for billing corrections in the policy's own scoped sentence (declared overwrite); no billing correction exists for the 2026-05-12 period. The base annual proration sentence is declared overwritten by the corrected term premium for riders on homeowner and rental property bases (real estate and monthly billing are restated unchanged); the whole-year 269.89 charge is wrong under the base sentence too. Work authorization (subject addon_benefit_authorization): covered_before_rider_benefit — d2 covered on Q2; one_open_rider_resolution — Q2 carries no repair, replacement or cash authorization. The base repair-or-replace and amount sentences are declared overwritten, the amount sentence with a scope sentence naming repair or replacement authorizations only. Removal (subjects addon_rider_removal, addon_premium_credit): rider_open_for_removal — removal allowed mid-term and status active; the one-credit gate is restated for removal credits. No time gate governs these subjects.

[Business-object card] Rider: the single Guest Unit Rider on the Gold homeowner contract. Correction object: the one prorated annual premium charge dated 2026-05-12 (payments and fees excluded by event type). Work object: the most recently placed request Q2 and its covered determination d2; Q1 already carries its 342.00 repair authorization. Removal object: the rider; retained premium = payments in the term less billing corrections; term benefit = 342.00 + the step-14 authorization.

[Seed rows] customers; homeplan_contracts (Gold, prior tier Silver, term 6, 5280 sq ft, ZIP 43221); homeplan_billing_entries (2024 and 2025 Silver premiums of 831.49 and the 2026 Gold premium of 950.29, each including the oversize surcharge, with ach payments 2024-02-13, 2025-02-03, 2026-01-12); lineplan_contracts and hvaccare_agreements (active); hvaccare_visit_events (completed tune-up 2025-04-20, missed visit 2026-04-18); addon_riders; addon_billing_entries (the whole-year charge, its card payment, visit fees 121.61 and 148.05 that agree with the visit-fee rule including Ohio sales tax); addon_service_requests (Q1 June routine, Q2 Saturday emergency); addon_claim_events (d1, a1 342.00 — the June work-authorization amount with the 0.90 maintenance share — and d2). No cache trap (rider premium_balance 0.00 equals the ledger). Automatic clauses checked: no renewal notice due, nothing unpaid, no rider in a waiting period, no haul-away owed on the new replacement because d2 documents no removal cost.

[Persona design] Marisol volunteers only the goal (cottage coverage off today, homeowner plan unchanged); gives phone 6145550163 and email only when verifying (ZIP spare); answers the reason and the "leave the main plan" question only when asked; if asked about the heat-pump job she wants it handled as Bridgewell normally does and declines cash; agrees passively to anything that must be settled, corrected or approved first; runs the handed-over removal with exactly the reference and amount given; closes when told the coverage was removed and the credit posted.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, email) -> riders -> homeowner contract -> rider billing, requests, claims -> homeowner billing -> line plan -> HVAC agreement -> HVAC visit events -> unlock+call post_rider_premium_correction_851994d3(rider, 2026-05-12, 56.44) -> unlock+call authorize_rider_work_f2a2f75a(Q2, replacement, 2902.20) -> unlock_user + customer calls remove_rider_with_credit_c919c4de(rider, 95.79).

[Verification] check_extended --task 0: EXTENDED OK; check_solvability --task 0: SOLVABILITY OK (3 calls, 3 base gates, 10 seed rows); check_compute --task 0: COMPUTE OK (15 factors, 13 cross-difficulty); replay_tasks: REPLAY OK (17 actions, closure 22 = initial 22); check_grounding: GROUNDING OK.

[Revision log — round 2, by audit item] F-3: the HVAC member uplift now reads the agreement level (Plus, Dual-System Plus or Premier / another level / none), every tier reachable. F-4: the billed-share method now follows the proration method in Bridgewell's rider rate schedule for the base property's region. F-5: the unearned-share method now follows the refund method in Bridgewell's filed contract terms for the property's region. F-6: the benefit-offset share now follows the claims terms in Bridgewell's filed contract terms for the property's region. O-10: the request limit now follows the base tier only, and the claim-history uplift was replaced by a per-component term limit and a maintenance share from the HVAC tune-up record. O-9: the prepayment ladder now leaves the published rate for on-time and late payers and rewards only payments 15 or more days early; the size tier now uses the homeowner tier's own oversize-home threshold. F-2: the removal waits on the latest covered request, the request the work-authorization rule settles. T0-O3: the charged premium is now the whole-year price on a mid-term add, an error under the base proration rule as well. T0-O2: the persona answers a heat-pump or cash question. T0-O4: the near-miss text above states exactly what the rule excludes. The Q1 request moved to June on the same heat pump, so the work authorization reads a same-component amount already authorized this term.

[Revision log — round 3, by item] Render note 1: the work-cost sentence now keeps every case of the retired base sentence — a covered determination that records no repair estimate, because the contractor found the component cannot be repaired or its parts cannot be obtained within the parts lead time, leads to replacement — and compute reads a missing estimate the same way; the heating request here records an estimate, so its outcome is unchanged. Render note 2: the removal-credit overwrites now name their scope (completed in round 4, below). Render note 5: the prepayment and autopay tiers now read only premium payments on the base homeowner contract, and the published rate applies when the rider's base is not a homeowner contract. The proration, refund and claims tiers are now worded as Bridgewell's own rate schedule and filed contract terms for the property's region rather than as state statutes. The visit fee booked on the Saturday heating request is dated the Monday it was collected, as the visit-fee rule now states for weekend requests.

[Revision log — round 4, by item] R3-1(a): the cancelled-base restatement in the removal-credit overwrites now carries every still-in-force part of the retired clause — the annual-billed or real estate base scope, the removal_credit_on_annual condition, the benefit net of reversals, the zero floor, no admin fee, and no credit on a monthly-billed base; the round-3 log above described that restatement as complete, which it was not. R3-1(b): the premium-correction policy now applies only to riders on homeowner or rental property bases, restates the real estate buyer-year billing formula and the monthly billing it does not touch, and books no correction for a real estate rider. O-15: the work-authorization rule now replaces when the determination records no repair estimate above zero, which is exactly what compute tests. Class sweep: every replaced_by now restates the still-in-force part of its retired clause (one credit per reason and period for other credits; the base tier's fee and same-visit test for rental and real estate riders; the per-request and term limits on cash). No input of this world changed.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rule prose, the tool schemas, the finder returns and her lines alone, the same three writes and figures (56.44; replacement 2902.20; 95.79) follow, every tier settled by a visible record.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Achterberg-Quaye, a retired high-school chemistry teacher in Upper Arlington, Ohio. You keep careful notes, speak in complete and slightly formal sentences, and you like to know that a thing has actually been done before you hang up. Your Bridgewell homeowner plan covers your house on Wickliffe Glen Road, and back in May you added coverage for the small backyard cottage where your mother-in-law was living. She moved into assisted living at the end of September, the cottage is now empty, and you have decided you no longer want to pay for the cottage coverage.

You open the call with only that: you would like the guest cottage coverage taken off your plan today, and you want the main homeowner plan on the house kept exactly as it is. You want it done on this call, not at renewal.

You are glad for the representative to take care of whatever on your account has to be handled to do this properly. If the representative tells you that something on the account has to be settled, corrected or approved before the cottage coverage can come off, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead; you never raise any such thing yourself and you do not ask in advance whether anything is pending. If the representative asks about the cottage heat pump job, you say you would like whatever Bridgewell normally does for that repair to go ahead, and if they offer you cash for it instead, you decline the cash. If they quote you a figure, you thank them and let them carry on; you do not know what any amount ought to be and you never suggest one. You understand that dropping a coverage is your own decision, so when the representative explains that the removal is a step you complete yourself and hands it to you, you carry it out straight away using exactly the rider reference and the credit amount they give you, and then you read back what it shows.

You do not volunteer personal details. Only when the representative asks you to confirm who you are do you give your phone number, 6145550163, and your email address, marisol.achterberg.quaye@fernhollow.net; if they say they need one more detail, you give your mailing ZIP code, 43221. If they ask why you are removing the cottage coverage, you say your mother-in-law has moved out and the cottage will sit empty for now. If they ask whether you want to change or cancel the main homeowner plan, you say no, please leave it exactly as it is. You do not have your paperwork in front of you and do not know any reference numbers; if asked for one, you say you don't have it handy and suggest they look you up by your phone number.

Once the representative tells you the cottage coverage has been removed and what credit was posted for it, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.
